paragraphs:
Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak. He was very old. He took myrtle branches and danced before the bride. R' (Zeira) said, “That old man is putting us to shame.” When he died, a pillar of fire separated them: Ketubbot, chapter 2, 17a; see R' Hanina bar Pappa. In Jerusalem Pe'ah, chapter 1, halakhah 1: he used to take his branch and praise the bride. R' Ze'ira would hide from him, saying, “Look at this old man, how he embarrasses us!” When he died, there were thunderclaps and lightning in the world for three hours. A heavenly voice went forth: “R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak, who performed acts of kindness, has died. Go forth to perform kindness for him.” Fire descended from heaven in the form of a fiery branch between his bier and the community. People said, “Look at this old man: his branch has stood by him.” In Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Kol ha-Tzelamim: when he died, the cedars of the Land of Israel were uprooted. They said that he used to take his branch and offer praise, and so forth; the rabbis murmured against him. R' Ze'ira said to them, “Leave him alone; that old man knows what he is doing,” and so forth. When he died, a heavenly voice went forth, saying, “Woe, for Shmuel bar Yitzhak, the doer of kindness, has died.” In Bereshit Rabbah, Hayyei Sarah, beginning of chapter 59: when he died, a storm wind went forth and uprooted all the fine trees. Why so? Because he used to gather branches from them and dance before the bride. The rabbis would say, “Why is he debasing the Torah?” R' Ze'ira said, and so forth.

R' Shmuel bar Yitzhak's maidservant said, “I used to wash my master's garments, and I never saw anything improper”: Jerusalem Helek, halakhah 2; Yevamot, chapter 2, halakhah 4. But in Rabbah, Kedoshim, chapter 24, this matter reads, “R' Yishmael son of R' Yitzhak … I used to attend to … his garments.” Mattenot Kehunah explains it as making the bed, whereas the Jerusalem Talmud commentary explains meshazzega as washing. The Jerusalem reading, that she washed, seems preferable to making the bed: in the testaments of R' Eliezer the Great it says that even if one has a thousand servants, one should make one's bed oneself, and presumably he would not have transgressed this. It is a scribal error and should read R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak. So it is in Yalkut, beginning of Kedoshim: this matter reads R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak. Yuhasin, end of letter yod, wrote: “R' Yishmael son of R' Yitzhak, like Elisha, no seminal emission was seen on his sheet.” The foregoing Midrash Kedoshim misled him. In Jerusalem Amar lahem ha-Memunnah, halakhah 7, R' Yishmael bar Yitzhak is likewise a scribal error. See above, R' Yishmael: meshazzega means washing. In Kiddushin, chapter 2, 54a, R' Yishmael bar Yitzhak is likewise a scribal error. In Zevahim 65b, “R' Zeira and R' Shimon bar Rav Yitzhak”—it seems to me a scribal error, and should read Shmuel.

“The father of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak taught”; see his entry. In Alfasi: “Abba, the father of R' Shmuel bar Yitzhak”; in Asheri: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzhak. See Zevahim 111b: bar Rav Yitzhak. R' Abba said to him: Sukkah 3a. He asked before R' Abba bar Mamal; see his entry at length. R' Avin reports in his name. Rav Adda bar Yitzhak—see his entry—was perhaps his brother. “So said R' Assi”; see immediately below. In R' Assi's name: Tamid 31b. R' Berekhiah son of R' Yehudah bar Simon reports in his name. R' Darmasti reports in his name. He asked Rav Huna: Eruvin 36a. He said in Rav Huna's name: Sukkah 3a; so it is in other books. He taught before Rav Huna: Megillah 8b and Bava Batra 113, beginning of side b. Rav Huna and R' Yirmeyah report in his name: the midrash at the beginning of the opening discourse of Eikhah; so too Jerusalem Hagigah, chapter 1, halakhah 7. This requires examination: would Rav Huna report in his pupil's name? I saw this matter in Yalkut Yirmeyah, chapter 9, remez 282: “Rav Huna, R' Yirmeyah, and R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak.” Perhaps it was corrected thus for the reason I have written.

R' Hoshaya was his son-in-law. And R' Zeira: Pesahim 72b. He asked R' Ze'ira, “What new teaching was there in the study hall?”: Jerusalem Amar lahem ha-Memunnah, halakhah 6. R' Haggai asked him. In R' Huna's name. He asked R' Hiyya bar Abba: Menahot 47a. He said to R. A. bar A. [ר״א ב״א], “My master, do you say this? So said Rav Assi”: Hullin 98a; see Jerusalem Gittin, chapter 3, halakhah 2. R' Hananyah reports in his name; R' Hinena reports in his name. He said in R' Yohanan's name: Hullin 116b. And R' Yasa. R' Yose son of R' Bun reports in his name. He asked R' Yaakov bar Aha: Jerusalem Yevamot, chapter 12. He sent R' Yaakov bar Aha to R' Hiyya bar Ba: Jerusalem Ba-Meh Ishah, halakhah 2. R' Yirmeyah and R' Meyasha report in his name: Jerusalem Shekalim, beginning of chapter 3, and Midrash Kohelet at “There is no good for a man that he should eat.” R' Yirmeyah asked R' Ze'ira before R' Shmuel bar Yitzhak's bier: Jerusalem Nazir, chapter 7, halakhah 1. R' Meyasha, the grandson of R' Yehoshua ben Levi, said to him. R' Pinhas.

In Rav's name: Yevamot 46a. He said in Rav's name: Ketubbot 26b; Niddah 47b; Berakhot 14b; Mo'ed Katan 12b. Megillah 8b: “R' Shmuel bar Yitzhak taught before Rav Huna … Rava said to him … rather, Rava said … Abaye said to him ….” It appears as though Rava spoke to R' Shmuel bar Yitzhak at the very time he taught before Rav Huna. But Rava did not see Rav Huna; see his entry. It therefore appears that we do not read “he said to him,” but “Rava said ….” Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi taught it thus: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzhak said; Rosh Hashanah 27, end of side a. In R' Shimon ben Elazar's name: Midrash Kohelet.
